Outlet: CNBC, published Thu Nov 5 2026 5:10 PM EST, updated 6:39 PM EST. By Sean Conlon, Gina Francolla, Christopher Hayes, Nick Wells
Magnificent 7 loses $1 trillion. The most eye-popping stats from Thursday's tech stock plunge

The Nasdaq Composite sank 5.5% into correction territory on Thursday, while the S&P 500 fell about 4.4% and the Dow dwindled roughly 1,833 points, or 3.4%. AI-linked technology shares led the decline as investors worried that data-center developments could slow after the midterm election results. The S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq posted their steepest one-day declines since the April 2025 tariff shock.

Stocks suffered a major sell-off on Thursday as investors' fears about a slowdown in the buildout of artificial intelligence rocked not only the trade itself but also the broader market. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite receded more than 5% and finished in correction territory alongside the small-cap Russell 2000 index. Those moves gave back the big gains seen in Wednesday's postelection rally and then some.

- Nasdaq Composite: worst single day since April 4, 2025 (when it fell 5.82%)
- S&P 500: worst single day since April 4, 2025 (when it declined 5.97%)
- Dow: worst day since April 4, 2025 (when it dropped more than 2,200 points, or 5.5%)
- "Magnificent Seven" lost more than $1 trillion in aggregate market cap, Nvidia leading at a loss of more than $440 billion
- Nvidia fell more than 9% and turned negative on the year, year-to-date fall now 2.6%
- VIX hit its highest level since March 31; gained 11.57 points, biggest point gain since April 4, 2025 (15.29 points)
- NYSE decliners outpaced advancers 2,344 to 416; Nasdaq 4,166 to 855
- All 11 S&P 500 sectors negative; information technology down 7.30%, worst since March 16, 2020 (13.92%); industrials fell 4.12%, worst since April 4, 2025 (6.29%)
- XLK fell 8.04%, worst since March 16, 2020 (13.81%); XLK traded more than 33 million shares vs 30-day average 9.2 million
- 174 (34.6%) of S&P 500 stocks 20%+ below 52-week high; 310 (61.6%) 10%+ below
- 59 (58.4%) of Nasdaq-100 stocks more than 20% off 52-week high; 72 (71.3%) more than 10% off
